1.why: A hedging clause ('assuming X remains steady') exists to qualify a projection; C restates it literally, A/B are off-topic. Purpose questions reward the inference.

2.why: 'its'' is never a word; 'their' signals the tested antecedent is singular; contraction vs possessive item usually keys to the possessive.

3.why: Dictionary meaning of 'motif'; B/C/D are adjacent literary terms (style, goal, plot twist) used as filler.

4.why: Rhetorical-synthesis 'fulfills the goal' items reward the option carrying both a fact and a stated purpose; B/C/D are bare details.

5.why: Professor-to-student email; C ('deadline extended') is not a concern at all, A/B are vaguer. D is the concrete complaint.

6.why: Listing three branches demonstrates breadth. A ('history') is unsupported by a list, B/D are grander claims than a list can carry.

7.why: Three of four options are dismissive of adaptation (ineffective / unnecessary / too costly) — a single-positive-versus-three-negatives spread almost always keys to the positive.

8.why: C puts a comma between subject and verb (never right); D changes number as a decoy. A closes a nonessential modifier before the verb.

9.why: The rainforest comparison is a biodiversity metaphor. A is a factual absurdity, B is the shallow reading, D is off-topic for a naming phrase.

10.why: Bleaching = expulsion of symbiotic algae under heat stress. A/C/D are all positive outcomes of a stressor, implausible by construction.

11.why: 'never previously documented' is superlative language; its rhetorical job is emphasis of severity. A/C are contrary to the phrase, B misreads 'scale' as 'novelty'.

12.why: A/B/C are absolutes ('too poor to salvage any', 'rarely', 'every household at the same moment'). D is the hedged evidence-based statement.

13.why: B/C/D each deny the premise wholesale (stocks never declined, overfishing played no role). A concedes the problem but limits the remedy — the standard cross-text key shape.

14.why: A/C/D are the three absolute readings (true cause / could not have occurred / no effect). B is the qualified middle.

15.why: 'students's' is never correct; the choice is plural possessive vs singular possessive vs plain plural. Plural possessive is the usual key when both plural forms are offered.

16.why: A/C/D are all evaluative put-downs; B is the neutral analytic purpose. Purpose questions rarely key to a criticism the passage does not make.

17.why: Pure guess on tense/agreement with no text; 'were' is the plural decoy, and present tense is the most common key in these items.

18.why: 'permitting' is a conditional availability hedge. B (rent) and D (construction) import unrelated topics; A misreads the sentence's function.

19.why: The quoted sentence explicitly juxtaposes cheap life with sacred property; C names that contrast. D contradicts the tone, B is structurally impossible for a single exclamatory line.

20.why: Data-support items key to the option citing both variables with figures. A and D cite one number and no relationship; B is C's numerical negation.

21.why: 'Ameliorate' means to improve; measure/ignore/predict are unrelated verbs.

22.why: EXCEPT items key to the false-sounding claim; space telescopes are not cheaper than ground-based ones, while B/C/D are standard Hubble facts a passage would state.

23.why: B is rude, C is argumentative, A defers without helping. D offers a concrete alternative — the cooperative reply these items reward.
